title: Sleepless Questions, Then Remembering
overview: A person in deep distress asks whether God has abandoned them for good, then turns to remembering how God once rescued Israel through the sea.

parts.label: A night with no comfort (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: The writer prays through a sleepless night with hands lifted, will not be comforted, and finds that even thinking about God only deepens the groaning. Memories of better years and of songs once sung in the night now seem to sharpen the pain.

parts.label: Six hard questions (vv. 7-9)
parts.note: The writer asks whether God has rejected them forever, whether God's faithful love and promises have run out, and whether anger has shut off mercy. Each question circles the same fear: that this silence from God is permanent.

parts.label: A turn toward memory (vv. 10-12)
parts.note: The Hebrew of verse 10 is unclear, so translations differ: some have the writer checking himself ('this is my weakness'), others have him choosing what to hold on to ('to this I will appeal'). Either way, the writer deliberately shifts from brooding on the present to recalling what God did long ago.

parts.label: The God who rescued (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: The Hebrew word in verse 13 can mean 'holiness' or 'the sanctuary,' the holy place of worship, so some translations say God's ways are holy and others say God's way is in the sanctuary. The writer then praises God as unlike any other god, the one who 'redeemed' (set free) the descendants of Jacob and Joseph, pointing to Israel's escape from slavery in Egypt.

parts.label: Through the sea (vv. 16-20)
parts.note: Images of shaking waters, thunder and lightning 'arrows' recall the crossing of the sea in the Exodus story, where God led the people like a flock through Moses and Aaron. God's path went through the water though no footprints could be seen, often read as God being at work even when unseen, and the psalm ends there without saying whether the writer's own trouble was resolved.

think: When the present feels dark, does remembering what carried you or others through hard times before help you, or does it sometimes make things harder?
